maria.s: Heads up — while validating the RBAC refactor in #product this morning I noticed Developer role can see org-level cost insights for projects they don't own. Not sure if this is a policy mapping bug or a migration flub.

devon.b: whoa, can you paste an example view or query that shows the exposure?

maria.s: Yep. I looked at the Cost Insights UI for org:acme-inc and opened the usage dashboard for project:research-42. Developers who are members of a different team could still load the dashboard.

maria.s: Query I ran against the analytics read view:
```
SELECT project_id, sum(token_cost) as total_cost
FROM billing_events
WHERE org_id = 'acme-inc' AND month = '2026-02'
GROUP BY project_id
```
Results returned multiple project rows even when my test user had only 'developer' scoped role on a single project.

sam.k: that's bad. Did the role->permission mapping change in the last deploy? IIRC we moved cost:read from project-level permission to a derived admin scope in the RBAC rewrite.

jen.p: I saw the RBAC PR (https://git.internal/redwood/rbac/pulls/412) — it included a migration that backfilled cost:read into role_definitions for legacy roles. Could be the migration applied org-level grants accidentally.

devon.b: ops-bot, can you surface the audit log for the migration step and who triggered the backfill? @ops-bot

ops-bot: audit-log: migration_backfill_rbac PR#412 applied by ci-system at 2026-03-10T03:12:45Z. Affected rows: 8,412. Query hash: a1b2c3. See /internal/audit/1799991111

sam.k: ok. immediate action: revoke the derived org-level cost grants and reapply as project scope. I'll open a rollback PR. Assigning to @sam.k and @devon.b for quick fix and verification.

devon.b: I'll run a targeted script to find principals with cost:read on org scope and remove where role != org-admin. Draft script:
```
DELETE FROM role_bindings
WHERE permission = 'cost:read' AND scope_type = 'org' AND role NOT IN ('org_admin','billing_admin')
```
Will run in dry-run first and post results.

maria.s: Please also add an alert for anomalous expansion of scope for sensitive permissions (cost:read, billing:export). This should be flagged in the RBAC CI checks.

jen.p: Agreed. Also let's verify KMS access didn't get broadened — some billing exports are encrypted with customer KMS keys. If role expansion allowed export, we need to audit key ACLs. @security-ops FYI.

ops-bot: runbook link: /runbooks/rbac_scope_incident. Notifying oncall @sam.k.

sam.k: I created hotfix PR https://git.internal/redwood/rbac/pulls/418 — it reverts the migration backfill and adds a migration check. Will request review from @devon.b. ETA 30m.

devon.b: Dry-run shows 132 bind entries would be removed. Seems low-risk. I'll schedule the removal now and validate with a test principal.

maria.s: After rollback, pls capture audit trail and send to compliance for the last 30 days. We need to know if any sensitive exports were downloaded by unintended principals.

jen.p: I'll run a report against S3 access logs + KMS decrypt logs for the same window. If anything anomalous, we escalate to incident response.

sam.k: Update: PR merged and deploy started. Rolling changes to role service. I'll post confirmation when deploy completes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rbac-service v2.3.1 -> SUCCESS at 2026-03-10T04:05:22Z

sam.k: Deploy complete. Devon, can you re-run the dry-run check and we can close the thread?

devon.b: Re-run done. 0 org-scoped cost:read entries remain for non-admin roles. Verified with test user 'alice_dev' and she no longer sees other projects' cost dashboards.

maria.s: Thanks team. Action items: 1) add RBAC CI gate to detect upward scope migration 2) add anomaly alert for billing permission expansion 3) compliance report (jen.p) 4) postmortem draft (maria.s). I can take the postmortem.

jen.p: I'll upload the compliance package by EOD.

ops-bot: incident-severity: low -> assigned

maria.s: Closing thread when reports are in. :lock:
